boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the XIII Army Corps and a Bridgehead Defense Force of three brigades without counts; the live field reads zero. Pemberton puts the line's defenders at about 4,000 with about twenty field pieces; Greene says there were not more than 5,000 in the trenches against fully double that number. NPS says three divisions of McClernand's corps moved out that morning.
claims.rationale: Defender and attacker figures differ in scope and source; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Greene says the trenches ran across the open, flat ground of a horseshoe bend behind a narrow but deep bayou, with bluffs 40 or 50 feet high on the far bank, and that work on them ran from May 12 to 15. Pemberton says the bayou was a serious obstacle but that the three-quarters of a mile between the works and the bridge was open and gave no cover.
claims.rationale: Inherited relative to the May 17 start; the works were built on Pemberton's orders beforehand and may be commander-created under a campaign boundary. No map verification or numerical effect.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says the Confederates burned the bridges after crossing, preventing close pursuit; Greene says the affair was over soon after 9 a.m.; Pemberton says he then ordered the army back within the Vicksburg defenses.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's statement that the battle sealed Vicksburg's fate is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,273 total (US 273; CS 2,000); the live field reads 2027 total (US 276; CS 1751;). NPS says about 1,800 were captured; Greene says 1,751 were made prisoners, 18 guns abandoned and over 1,400 small arms thrown away, with Federal losses of 273 killed and wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The Confederate figures are dominated by prisoners and are not an opening strength.

open_questions: Gates's and Cockrell's reports, McClernand's and Lawler's reports and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
